Anika: Quick question. Partner baby arrived early. I'm starting parental leave next week but my role is part of a two‑person job share. Can I request an extension later while on leave, and how do we handle coverage now?

Rory (People Ops): Congrats! You can request an extension while on leave; submit an extension request in the HR portal at least 2 weeks before your planned return. For immediate coverage, manager should either reassign duties internally or submit a finance intake for a temporary contractor.

Anika: If I extend unpaid, do benefits keep running?

Leah (Benefits): Employer health contributions continue during paid leave only. For unpaid extensions, benefits pause unless you elect to continue coverage and pay the employee portion (we'll send COBRA or local continuation options). Submit your extension early so we can run the benefits impact notice.

Tom (Hiring): For coverage: if you want interviews paused, mark candidates "on hold". If you prefer a temp to cover coding reviews, submit a short-term req and tag "parental-backfill." We can often approve a 3-month contractor quickly.

Anika: Thanks. One more: manager asked about whether we keep headcount open if teammate also goes on leave later in quarter. What's policy?

Rory (People Ops): Headcount stays with the org. If two people on same FTE take overlapping leave, we don't reduce headcount automatically. Managers decide to backfill temporarily vs. redistribute work. Finance intake will be needed for contractor budget if you want extra capacity.

hr-bot: Links: leave portal: https://redwood.example.company/hr/parental-leave. Finance intake: https://redwood.example.company/finance/intake.

Anika: Filing extension option now and I'll tell manager about finance intake. Appreciate it.

(End of thread)
